cards.text: Mark 14 opens with a countdown. The Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread are two days away, and everybody's getting ready for a feast. But the chief priests and scribes? Friend, they are getting ready for something ELSE.

cards.question: Two days before the Passover, the chief priests and scribes are looking for a way to welcome Jesus to the feast.

cards.text: They're looking for a covert way to arrest Jesus and kill Him, and their plan comes with fine print. "But not during the feast," they say.

cards.question: The chief priests and scribes say they won't arrest Jesus during the feast, or there may be a ___ among the people.

cards.text: Meanwhile, Jesus is in Bethany. He's reclining at the table in the home of a man called Simon the Leper.
Then a woman comes in with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume, made of pure nard. This is NOT the bottle you crack open on some random Tuesday.

cards.question: In Simon the Leper's home, what does the woman do with her alabaster jar of perfume?

answers.text: Breaks it open and pours it on Jesus' head
Hands it to Simon as a gift for the house
Sets it down unopened at Jesus' feet

cards.text: Not everybody in the room is a fan. Some of those present get indignant and say to one another, "Why this waste of perfume?"

cards.question: The people grumbling about the woman say her perfume could have been sold. For how much?
The grumblers say the money from the perfume could have been given to the ___, and they scold the woman.

cards.text: So now she's getting scolded from every side of the table. Then Jesus speaks up: "Leave her alone; why are you bothering her? She has done a beautiful deed to Me."

cards.question: Jesus tells the grumblers they'll always have the poor with them, and they can help them whenever they want. What does He say about Himself?

answers.text: They won't always have Him with them
They should serve Him before the poor
He'll take care of the poor Himself

cards.question: Jesus says the woman has done what she could. What does He say her perfume did?

answers.text: Anointed His body in advance of His burial
Marked Him as the king who was coming
Made Him ready for the Passover meal

cards.question: Jesus says that wherever the gospel is preached in all the world, what this woman did will be told in memory of her.

cards.text: And look at me, a cookie stamper on a cookie planet, telling her story to you right now. Promise KEPT, friend.
Meanwhile, those chief priests are about to get a visitor. One of the Twelve walks right up to them, ready to betray Jesus.

cards.question: Which one of the Twelve goes to the chief priests to betray Jesus?
The chief priests are ___ to hear what Judas Iscariot has come to do, and they promise to give him ___.

cards.text: So Judas begins to look for an opportunity to betray Jesus. The feast is coming, friend, and this story is far from over.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: "Mark 14 opens with a countdown." / "The Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread are two days away, and everybody's getting ready for a feast." / "But the chief priests and scribes?" / "Friend, they are getting ready for something ELSE." The limit for an opening card is three.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card tells that the chief priests and scribes are looking for a covert way to arrest Jesus and kill Him. That comes from Mark 14:1, but the card cites only Mark 14:2. It should cite Mark 14:1-2.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card opens with "she's getting scolded," which retells Mark 14:5 ("And they scolded her"). It cites only Mark 14:6, so it should cite Mark 14:5-6.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "Scolded from every side of the table" stretches the text. Mark 14:4-5 says only that "some of those present" were indignant and scolded her. This is narration, not one of Papa Dorin's jokes.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke about Papa Dorin telling the story. It adds no part of the passage, because Mark 14:9 was already covered on card 14. The card is filler in a short passage and does not move the baker forward. Its joke should ride along on a card that tells part of the passage, or the card should be cut.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: "Meanwhile" makes Judas's visit to the chief priests sound like it happens at the same time as the anointing. Mark 14:10 says "Then," which puts it afterward.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.
